Straight-line distances between two sets of points

Source: R/location.R
distance_matrix.Rd

Every pair of an origin and a destination at most max_distance metres apart in a straight line, with the distance. It needs no network, and its result is a table that locate_facilities() and floating_catchment() take in travel_times, for the cases in which the service standard is a distance (a water point within 1 km) or the streets of the area are not mapped well enough to route on.

Usage

distance_matrix(origins, destinations, max_distance)

Arguments

origins, destinations

The points: a data.frame with id, lon and lat, or a POINT sf with an id column.

max_distance

The longest distance kept, in metres (the pairs with distance <= max_distance).

Value

A table with one row per pair, ordered as the origins and, within each, as the destinations: from_id, to_id and distance (metres).

Tables are tibbles by default; options(peabiru.output = "data.frame") gives base data.frames and options(peabiru.output = "data.table") gives data.tables (see peabiru-package).

Details

The distance is the great-circle one on a sphere of radius 6,367,450 m, the same that measures the streets of a network, and is the same on every platform. A pair at distance 0 is a pair. Only the pairs within max_distance are computed, so two large sets of points with a short distance take little time and memory.

See also

Other facility location: allocate_budget()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
points <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "spo_points.csv"))
near <- distance_matrix(points, points, max_distance = 800)
head(near)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   from_id         to_id           distance
#>   <chr>           <chr>              <dbl>
#> 1 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c00fffff       0 
#> 2 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c007ffff     352.
#> 3 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c077ffff     341.
#> 4 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c03bffff     359.
#> 5 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c033ffff     624.
#> 6 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c067ffff     682.
# the two points with the most residents within 800 m of them
locate_facilities(NULL, points, points, model = "max_cover", n_facilities = 2,
                  cutoff = 800, demand_colname = "population",
                  travel_times = near)$sites
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   id                lon   lat order marginal cumulative
#>   <chr>           <dbl> <dbl> <int>    <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 89a8100c023ffff -46.6 -23.6     1    39445      39445
#> 2 89a8100c397ffff -46.6 -23.5     2     6828      46273
